summary: Tuvalu's mission to the UN says visas are not required for stays in Tuvalu of up to 30 days, and that entry permits for a maximum one-month stay are issued on arrival. Under Tuvalu's Immigration Regulations 2014, citizens of the countries listed in Schedule 1, among them the United Kingdom, Fiji and Samoa, pay no visitor's permit fee and others pay $100 (the regulations do not name the currency) unless the Minister waives it. Under the EU–Tuvalu visa waiver agreement, which does not apply to the United Kingdom and Ireland, citizens of the Union may stay for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tuvalu?
faq.answer: No visa is needed for stays of up to 30 days: Tuvalu's mission to the UN says visas are not required for stays in Tuvalu of up to 30 days, and that entry permits for a maximum one-month stay are issued on arrival, provided you have a valid passport (at least for 6 months from the date of arrival), sufficient funds, proof of accommodation and a return or onward ticket. Under the Immigration Regulations 2014, citizens of the countries listed in Schedule 1, among them the United Kingdom, Malaysia, the Republic of Korea, Fiji, Kenya and Jamaica, pay no visitor's permit fee; others pay $100 (the regulations do not name the currency) unless the Minister waives it. The EU–Tuvalu visa waiver agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the Union for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period; it does not apply to the United Kingdom and Ireland.

faq.question: How much does the Tuvalu visitor's permit cost?
faq.answer: The Immigration Regulations 2014 set a visitor's permit fee of $100 (they do not name the currency) for citizens of countries not listed in Schedule 1, unless the Minister waives it; citizens of the countries listed, among them the United Kingdom, Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Tonga, Malaysia and the Republic of Korea, pay no fee. The UK Foreign Office says there are no ATMs in Tuvalu, that credit or debit card payments are not accepted, and to bring enough Australian dollars in cash for the duration of your trip.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than a month?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says that to stay longer than one month you must get an extension from the Department of Immigration in Funafuti. Under the Immigration Regulations 2014, the Principal Immigration Officer may extend a visitor's permit for up to 30 days, upon payment of a fee of $100 if no employment or business activities are permitted, or $200 if the visitor intends to engage in business or employment; the regulations do not name the currency.

faq.question: Are there ATMs or card payments in Tuvalu?
faq.answer: No. The UK and Canada both say there are no ATMs in Tuvalu and that credit and debit card payments are not accepted. The UK says to bring enough Australian dollars in cash with you for the duration of your trip.
